interpretation: The reference count-only LLM baseline has higher forecast error than the public plain mechanistic model on both selected worlds. Four of six observed counts exactly match the reference while raw traces differ. These runs motivate sharing a full-trace forecaster in an actual constructor comparison, not claiming a novel instrument or an impossibility of identifying the current model.
measurement_boundary: The raw-voltage differences are noiseless trajectory differences and may include spike phase shifts. Their RMSE is not a proof of mechanism identifiability, robustness to stochastic channel noise, or a successful discovered model.
held_out_scope: Native six-protocol scoring set per world. The untouched native package has some protocol overlap with its acquisition menu; these scores are not asserted to be six wholly unseen protocols per episode.
decision: Keep the new native partial-observation carrier; do not use these weak baseline scores as method evidence and do not scale up.
next_requirement: Implement a concrete experiment-program constructor with its core learning/update steps executable, sharing a full-voltage mechanistic forecaster and identical native control access with its comparisons. Test whether source-learned transformations produce useful new temporal experiments on unseen mechanisms beyond same-prior continuous design and applicable MDA-style inference. Do not infer a need for new experiments from a count-only forecaster discarding available trace information; do not treat menu selection, a researcher-provided conditioning template, or undefined inverse-planning calls as the learned contribution. Preserve the broad novelty and multi-core-task objective; no long GPU work is warranted yet.
